_note: Limits & honesty page content (FR-SET-3, doc 11 §5.9, doc 14 §4). Statically imported by src/features/handbook/content/limits.ts and validated at load. kind: real = public data or published evidence; measured = measured by the user in this app; simulated = synthetic; modeled = a model or an assumption built on published values; demo = our own formula or parameter; experimental = not validated or not built. availability: absent = in this build; 'unavailable' = designed but not working in this build; 'not-built' = described but not implemented. The rPPG validation table is not here (docs/VALIDATION.md does not exist yet): rppgValidation gives the honest default.

dataKinds.label: NOAA GOES proton flux
dataKinds.detail: Live 5-minute proton flux from NOAA SWPC, converted to the NOAA S-scale. Offline, ARGUS shows the last cached copy or a bundled snapshot with its age.

dataKinds.label: NASA DONKI solar particle events
dataKinds.detail: Event list from NASA's DONKI space-weather catalog. Currently unavailable in this build.

dataKinds.label: NASA OSDR pre-flight blood values
dataKinds.detail: Real, anonymised pre-flight blood counts (OSD-569) and metabolic panel values (OSD-575) of commercial astronauts, used as pre-flight anchors for the fictional crew and for lab reference ranges. They are not the fictional crew's own values.

dataKinds.label: Published limits and evidence
dataKinds.detail: NASA-STD-3001 limits, NASA human-research risk pages and the peer-reviewed findings behind the space rules. Every number links to its entry in the source registry, with its status (verified or partial).

dataKinds.label: Camera pulse
dataKinds.detail: Measured with your camera in the Lab (POS method), with a quality score. Video stays on this device. Only the number is saved.

dataKinds.label: Reaction Self-Test
dataKinds.detail: Measured by you on this device, modeled on NASA's 3-minute PVT-B.

dataKinds.label: Manual entries and imports
dataKinds.detail: Values you type in or import from a file are labeled MEASURED. They are compared with the selected crew member's simulated baseline.

dataKinds.label: Crew members and their daily readings
dataKinds.detail: The four crew members are fictional. Their baselines, daily readings, noise and scenarios are synthetic, and every screen that shows them carries the SIMULATED DATA badge.

dataKinds.label: Cabin sensors
dataKinds.detail: Cabin CO₂, temperature and humidity are a simulated sensor stream; the limits they are judged against are real.

dataKinds.label: Pre-mission career doses
dataKinds.detail: Each crew member's radiation dose before this mission is a simulated value.

dataKinds.label: Solar particle event replay
dataKinds.detail: REPLAY — a synthetic S2-class profile (demo), not a recorded event. It is never shown as real or live.

dataKinds.label: Cosmic-ray dose rates
dataKinds.detail: Published dose-equivalent measurements (ISS, Mars cruise, lunar surface, Mars surface) applied to the mission profiles as assumptions. They are dose equivalent, while the career limit is an effective dose.

dataKinds.label: Modeled solar-event dose
dataKinds.detail: Modeled — illustrative. Real crew dose comes from personal dosimeters.

dataKinds.label: Mars-transit comms delay
dataKinds.detail: Modeled delay (demo): a demo profile of how the one-way delay grows during the transit, not derived from a trajectory.

dataKinds.label: Shelter advisory
dataKinds.detail: A demo policy that maps the S-scale to an advisory. Real shelter calls come from the mission's radiation specialists.

dataKinds.label: Readiness index, points and streaks
dataKinds.detail: A demo formula computed from open flags and routine adherence, not an Integrated Medical Model output.

dataKinds.label: Rule band edges marked demo
dataKinds.detail: Band edges marked Demo parameter are our own choices for this prototype; they are not clinical or NASA limits.

dataKinds.label: Personal baseline tuning constants
dataKinds.detail: The thresholds, spread floors and the expected in-flight sleep shift of the personal baseline engine are tuning choices for this prototype.

dataKinds.label: Measurement quality and staleness
dataKinds.detail: Camera quality thresholds, re-measure timing and the assumed camera field of view are our own choices.

dataKinds.label: Face fluid-shift index
dataKinds.detail: Built: experimental, not validated; the reference is the first scan on this device; trend only — it never raises Watch or Act.

dataKinds.label: Respiration rate from the camera
dataKinds.detail: Experimental and not built in this version.

notMedicalDevice: ARGUS is a hackathon prototype for decision support. It is not a diagnostic or certified medical device and gives no drug doses. Its actions are limited to re-measuring, telling the Crew Medical Officer, sending a report to the flight surgeon and following a listed protocol.
nonGoals: Not a diagnostic or certified medical device; no drug dosing.
No claim that rPPG or the face index replace clinical instruments.
Simulated crew data is synthetic; real NASA datasets are used for pre-flight anchors and environment.
No real identity/security system (demo PINs); design notes describe what flight software would need.

knownGaps.label: Identity and access
knownGaps.detail: The demo uses a role picker and a shared PIN. Flight software would use the agency identity system.

knownGaps.label: Encryption at rest
knownGaps.detail: Records in the browser database are not encrypted. Encrypting them (WebCrypto AES-GCM) is future work.

knownGaps.label: Camera pulse validation
knownGaps.detail: No paired validation against a reference device has been done yet.

knownGaps.label: Clinical review of demo thresholds
knownGaps.detail: Band edges and baseline constants marked Demo parameter are our own choices and have not been reviewed by clinicians or flight surgeons.

knownGaps.label: Real radiation dose
knownGaps.detail: Turning space-weather flux into dose inside a vehicle needs transport codes and vehicle geometry. ARGUS does not do that; flight use would read dose from personal dosimeters and shelter calls from radiation specialists.

knownGaps.label: Live device adapters
knownGaps.detail: Device import from files is planned and not in this build. Formats like CSA's Bio-Monitor smart shirt or the ARCHeR actigraph would plug in via an adapter; no live adapter is built.

knownGaps.label: Connection to NASA's crew health data platform
knownGaps.detail: ARGUS uses a FHIR-style data model so it could feed a platform like CHP-IDSP; no such connection exists.

rppgValidation.placeholder: No paired validation against a reference device has been done yet.
